selection_pending: Main Agent must select mode with an explicit reason based on scope, quality, recovery and cost; no automatic matrix expansion.

selection.reason: For this read-only reviewer task, fixed host read/write boundaries and immediate denial suffice. Sandbox has higher three-run mean score and lower mean task time. Neither mode made any approval request, so the observed timing difference is stochastic task behavior, not measured guardian overhead. Approve-for-me offers no demonstrated benefit here; the independent triggered probe confirms local guardian compatibility and an added 3.569 seconds for one no-op approval, not a repeated overhead estimate.
limitations: Both profiles require read-only runtime dependencies outside the project. Private sandbox empty namespace permits ephemeral writes, while host canaries and fixed scratch boundary are enforced; this is not literal virtual-path-only writing.
Normal review instances contain no escalation request in either mode; guardian decision quality and overhead when frequently invoked remain unmeasured.
One invalid-patch tool failure in approve-for-me was corrected; no evidence/findings were lost during recovery. No API failures occurred in these six instances.

Historical sandbox observations precede the revised mode-first priority; reused only under identical frozen task, prompt, model, effort, release and profile. They are not an interleaved randomized causal experiment.
The frozen Code Standards prompt explicitly prohibits requesting escalation. These mode runs characterize this no-escalation reviewer workload, not workloads needing approved out-of-scope actions.
